Zoe H: During a scheduled compliance scan I found a build log in our CI cache that contains a full service account JSON (plaintext). File: `ci-cache://runner-17/build-982/logs/step-4.log`. Looks like a test runner leaked `service_account.key`. Need immediate rotation + containment. @Akshay can you triage?
Akshay: Ack. Short checklist: 1) prune the cache object 2) disable the exposed key 3) rotate vault refs if present 4) tighten runner RBAC and redact logs. Can you paste the log snippet?
Zoe H: Snippet: `... DEBUG: writing credentials: {"type":"service_account","project_id":"redwood-prod","private_key_id":"cafebabe1234","private_key":"-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----...` found at 2026-06-15T07:22:13Z.
Priya S: Oof. Likely a test helper wrote a credential file and `cat`-ed it. Immediate actions: remove cache object, revoke key, search Vault for `private_key` occurrences, and add a runner hook to scrub secrets from logs.
Ben J: I'll run repo/CI job search: `rg "private_key|service_account" .ci/ scripts/ || true` and `aws s3 rm ci-cache://runner-17/build-982 --recursive` (conceptual). Also add a short-term Vault policy denying the CI runner SA from reading `secret/` paths.
Jamie P: Platform: we can push an emergency runner patch to mount `/no-log` and set `GHA_STEP_COMMANDS_REDIRECT_OUTPUT=1` to avoid leaking to logs. Also we should add a log-redaction filter in the agent to redact base64 blobs and PEM blocks. I'll open the hotfix PR.
ci-bot: Cache object removed and snapshot taken -> s3://incidents/4098765432/cache-snap-2026-06-15.tgz
sre-bot: Created alert `ci.leak.scan.4098765432` and routed to #incidents. Pager oncall.
Akshay: Disabled key cafebabe1234 at 2026-06-15T07:37:02Z. Fingerprint: SHA256:CAFEBABE0001. Deleting key now and creating a replacement with least-priv. Will wrap new key with our KMS and store in Vault at `secret/ci/runner/serviceacct-v2`.
Zoe H: Vault check: `secret/ci/test-fixtures/` contains `sa_json` files with raw JSON. Looks like integration tests pushed real creds. Marking those paths as compromised.
Priya S: Run `vault kv get -format=json secret/ci/test-fixtures | jq -r .data.data.sa_json` and rotate. Also set a policy `policy-ci-runner-redact` that denies read on `secret/` for the `ci-runner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` until rotation finishes.
Ben J: I've pushed patch to CI to replace any `echo $SA_JSON` with `printf '[REDACTED]'` and added a pre-step that fails if `private_key` pattern is present: `if rg -q "private_key" $FILES; then echo "Found secret"; exit 1; fi`. PR opened.
Jamie P: Also pushing KMS IAM tighten: remove broad `group:devs@` binding on the KMS key used for envelope; only `serviceAccount:vault-sa@redwood` + `platform-ops@redwood` should have decrypt. Adding an org policy to forbid external members.
Akshay: New SA created `ci-runner-service-temp@project`, key generated, wrapped with KMS and written to Vault `secret/ci/runner/serviceacct-v2`. Rotated consumers and restarted runners. Adding TTL 1h on the new key.
Legal: Please prepare notification draft; was there any external access?
Zoe H: Quick audit: KMS logs + GCP audit show no decrypt/unwrap calls from external IPs. Access was internal from runner IPs. No sign of exfil yet. Exported logs to incident doc.
Priya S: Postmortem actions: 1) enforce pre-ingest/CI lint to block private keys 2) run a one-off sweep of CI caches for patterns 3) require all test creds to be ephemeral WIF or mocked 4) add log redaction agent to runners. I will own the sweep.
Jamie P: I'll own runner hotfix and the KMS IAM tidy. Ben, please follow up on automation to rotate any affected Vault paths.
Ben J: Will open automation PR for rotating `secret/ci/test-fixtures` to `.v2` and updating tests to use mocked creds.
Akshay: I'll produce the timeline for audit and add commands we ran. Deletion confirmed at 2026-06-15T07:42:10Z.
Zoe H: Partner/customer impact: none identified. CS/Legal looped. Leaving thread open for 48h monitoring. :lock:
